text: Drosophila Dicer-2 generates siRNAs from long double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), while Dicer-1 produces miRNAs from pre-miRNA. Purified Dicer-2 efficiently cleaves pre-miRNA, but inorganic phosphate and the partner protein R2D2 inhibit this. Dicer-2 has C-terminal RNase III domains mediating RNA cleavage and an N-terminal helicase motif of unclear function. Dicer-2 is a dsRNA-stimulated ATPase hydrolyzing ATP to ADP; ATP hydrolysis is required to process long dsRNA, but not pre-miRNA. Wild-type Dicer-2, unlike an ATP-hydrolysis-defective mutant, generates siRNAs faster than it dissociates from a long dsRNA substrate. The authors propose the Dicer-2 helicase domain uses ATP to generate many siRNAs from a single dsRNA molecule before dissociating.
